outcome: No source I could open reports a prime p with 47^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p^2) since 26 January 2024, so the existence question is still open. The only base-47-specific movement found is a search bound: 1.07 x 10^14 (OEIS A278611, dated 23 Nov 2016) was superseded by 2 x 10^14 (Fischer's table, last updated 1 Sep 2025; an unsigned OEIS comment) at a date I could not pin down, and a 30 Sep 2026 Fischer table states a conflicting search limit of 4.75 x 10^12.
problem_asks: Existence only: whether there is at least one prime p with 47^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p^2). Any witness must be a prime p other than 47, since 47^46 is 0 mod 47^2. The bullet asks for no count, no infinitude, and no other part. Wikipedia's current list gives it as a bare question, 'Are there any Wieferich primes in base 47?', linking to the Wieferich prime article, with no nested sub-bullets.

events.what_happened: OEIS A278611 ('Bases b > 1 that set a new record for the size of the smallest base-b Wieferich prime', submitted by Felix Frohlich, 23 Nov 2016) comments that 'any Wieferich primes in bases 47 and 72 are larger than 1.07*10^14 (cf. Fischer)'. The attribution is to Richard Fischer's fermatquotient.com table. Fetched as a live page; no later revision of this comment was visible.
events.revisions: Entry submitted 23 Nov 2016; the fetched page showed no later edit to this comment. The earliest appearance of the 1.07 x 10^14 figure itself may be earlier than this entry.
events.delivers: A computational search bound, not a result on existence: if a base-47 Wieferich prime exists, it exceeds 1.07 x 10^14 (per Fischer's search as cited). Restricted to the stated search range; says nothing about primes above it.
events.remains: Whether any base-47 Wieferich prime exists above 1.07 x 10^14, and whether there are infinitely many. The bound does not touch the infinitude question.
events.directly_checkable: Any candidate prime p can be tested by computing pow(47, p-1, p*p) == 1 in any big-integer library. I did not rerun Fischer's search.
events.doubts: The bound is a second-hand citation inside an OEIS comment. Its underlying search is Fischer's, and the same site later states a higher bound (see event fischer-table-2e14-bound). The 1.07 x 10^14 figure is therefore superseded on the same site.
events.direction: No object. A search with no hit cuts neither way on existence; it is consistent with the question being open.
people: Richard Fischer (author of the cited table)

events.what_happened: Richard Fischer's table FermQ_Sort.txt (Fermat quotients / Wieferich table for bases 2 to 1052; footer dated 01.09.2025, signed Richard Fischer) lists base 47 as '47 keine gefunden' (none found) and states, in German, that bases whose largest prime factor is at most 149 are searched to 2.00E+14, while the remaining bases are searched to 6.46E+13. Base 47 has largest prime factor 47, so by that rule it is searched to 2 x 10^14; applying the rule to base 47 is my inference from the header text. The same figure appears as an unsigned OEIS A039951 comment: 'a(47) > 2*10^14, a(72) > 2*10^14 (see Fischer's tables)'. A second Fischer table, FermQ_Sorg.txt (bases 2 to 10125; footer dated 30.09.2026), has a row '47,' with no prime after it and states 'Die Basen sind gegenwaertig durchsucht bis 4.75E+12' (bases are currently searched to 4.75E+12). That conflicts with 2 x 10^14.
events.revisions: The page carrying 2.00E+14 was last updated 01.09.2025. The OEIS line carrying 2 x 10^14 is unsigned and undated. The earlier figure 1.07 x 10^14 is dated 23 Nov 2016 (event oeis-a278611-2016-bound). The date the 2 x 10^14 figure first appeared is not established, so I cannot say whether it falls inside the window.
events.delivers: A finite search: per Fischer's table, if any base-47 Wieferich prime exists it exceeds 2 x 10^14. Restricted to the stated search; says nothing about larger primes. The 4.75 x 10^12 statement, if taken at face value, would give a much weaker bound, so the table is not self-consistent.
events.remains: Whether any base-47 Wieferich prime exists above 2 x 10^14 (or above 4.75 x 10^12, if that statement governs), and whether there are infinitely many.
events.time_since_posted: about 13 months since the table's 01.09.2025 update; the undated OEIS line's age is unknown
events.directly_checkable: Any candidate p is checkable by pow(47, p-1, p*p) == 1. Fischer's search program is not on the pages I read, so the search itself was not reproduced.
events.doubts: (1) The two Fischer tables give inconsistent search limits: 2.00E+14 (01.09.2025) against 'currently searched to 4.75E+12' (30.09.2026). (2) The 2 x 10^14 figure has no date in OEIS. (3) The rule that applies 2 x 10^14 to base 47 is my inference from German header text, not an explicit statement about base 47. (4) A search-snippet figure of 1.4 x 10^14 for base 47 appeared in search results but on no page I opened. (5) No paper, referee report or independent rerun of this search was found.
events.direction: No object. Search with no hit; consistent with the question being open, cuts neither way on existence.
people: Richard Fischer (maintainer of the fermatquotient.com tables)

events.what_happened: OEIS A338646 (Felix Frohlich, submitted 22 Apr 2021; a(19) and a(20) added 1-2 Jul 2021) lists primes p with 47^(p-1) ≡ 1 + A*p (mod p^2) where |A/p| sets a new record low, using the 'nearness' notion of Dorais and Klyve. Terms shown: 2, 3, 5, 19, 37, 47, 38693, 44657, 148091, 178621, 692521, 4584379, 262148693, 347850691, 502176491, 1139746919, 1387837067, 5291181761, 92653098679, 202259581243. Its comments say 47 is the smallest b with no known base-b Wieferich prime, and that the sequence terminates at a base-47 Wieferich prime if one exists.
events.revisions: Submitted 22 Apr 2021; a(19) 1 Jul 2021; a(20) 2 Jul 2021; all by Frohlich.
events.delivers: Nothing on existence. It is a ranking of near-misses for base 47, with a remark that the sequence would end at a base-47 Wieferich prime if one exists. The remark is conditional on existence.
events.directly_checkable: The listed terms can be recomputed with a modular-exponentiation loop; the entry gives a PARI program. I did not rerun it.
events.doubts: The listed term 47 cannot satisfy the congruence as written, since 47^46 is 0 mod 47^2 and not 1 + A*47 for an integer A. The entry's convention for the base itself is unexplained on the page I read.
events.direction: No object. A ranking of near-misses; it does not cut either way.
people: Dorais and Klyve (definition of nearness, cited)

events.what_happened: F. G. Dorais and D. Klyve, 'A Wieferich prime search up to 6.7 x 10^15', Journal of Integer Sequences 14 (2011), article 11.9.2. Reports a faster search for base-2 Wieferich primes, finding no others below 6.7 x 10^15 beyond 1093 and 3511, and introduces the near-Wieferich measure later used for base 47 in OEIS A338646. The abstract, as read via summary, also reports no Fibonacci-Wieferich primes.
events.delivers: Base 2 only: no Wieferich prime p < 6.7 x 10^15 other than 1093 and 3511. Says nothing about base 47 in any part I could read.
events.doubts: Full text not read: the JIS PDF returned HTTP 503 and the HTML version HTTP 404. The abstract was read through a summary of the dorais.org page, and the bound symbol was stripped in that summary, so the bound is taken from the title.
events.direction: Base 2 result; no object for base 47.

events.what_happened: N. A. Carella, 'Results for Wieferich Primes', arXiv:1712.08166 (v1 21 Dec 2017; v2 5 May 2018). Gives an asymptotic count of primes p with v^(p-1) ≡ 1 mod p^2 in short intervals for a general base v. The only search result stated in the abstract is base 2 up to 10^15 (two primes found), and it predicts heuristically that another base-2 prime exists in [10^15, 10^40].
events.delivers: A heuristic prediction for base 2. No base-47 result in the abstract; the 53-page text was not read.
events.doubts: A heuristic prediction is not evidence of existence in any base, including base 47.
events.direction: Base 2 heuristic. Cuts toward existence for base 2 only; nothing for base 47.

events.what_happened: N. Fellini and M. Ram Murty, 'Wieferich primes in number fields and the conjectures of Ankeny-Artin-Chowla and Mordell', arXiv:2508.08472 (v1 11 Aug 2025; v2 11 Feb 2026, labelled 'Final version'). Works with a general base alpha in a number field. Unconditionally, an AAC equivalence in terms of eps^(p-1) ≡ 1 mod p^2. Conditionally, on Masser's abc for number fields, or on finitely many base-alpha super-Wieferich primes, they show infinitely many base-alpha non-Wieferich primes with a lower bound of order log x / log log x.
events.revisions: v1 11 Aug 2025; v2 11 Feb 2026 'Final version' (17 pages).
events.delivers: About non-Wieferich prime ideals in number fields, with the infinitude claims conditional on abc or on finiteness of super-Wieferich primes. The unconditional part is an AAC equivalence. Nothing asserts a base-47 Wieferich prime, and the base 47 case is not named in the abstract.
events.remains: Existence of any base-47 Wieferich prime; the paper does not claim it.

checked_by.who: Journal of Number Theory (per a search snippet: volume 285 (2026), accepted 30 Jan 2026; not verified on the journal page)

events.doubts: The infinitude results rest on hypotheses the paper does not prove (abc for number fields, or finiteness of super-Wieferich primes). The journal acceptance date comes from a snippet I did not verify.
events.direction: Non-Wieferich direction: infinitely many non-Wieferich prime ideals under conditional hypotheses. No statement that base-47 Wieferich primes exist.

events.what_happened: H. Graves and B. Weiss, 'The abc conjecture implies infinitely many non-Wieferich places for fixed bases in number fields', arXiv:2503.19144 (submitted 24 Mar 2025; one version, 15 pages). Under abc, proves analogues of Graves-Murty and Ding results for number fields; Ding's result is said to hold for all bases in the rings of integers of imaginary quadratic fields, with 31 explicit exceptions. The abstract also cites Silverman's abc-conditional bound of order log x non-Wieferich primes below x.
events.delivers: Conditional on abc: infinitely many non-Wieferich places for fixed bases in number-field analogues, with explicit exceptions. Nothing about the existence of Wieferich primes in base 47.
events.remains: Existence of any base-47 Wieferich prime, and whether Wieferich primes exist at all in a given base.
events.doubts: Conditional on abc. A search-snippet claim that the paper says it is unknown whether infinitely many non-Wieferich primes exist for some non-unit base was not in the abstract I read; that claim is unverified.
events.direction: Non-Wieferich direction, conditional on abc, in number fields. No object.

events.what_happened: R. Li and J. Zhao, 'Non-Wieferich property of prime ideals and a conjecture of Erdos', arXiv:2601.12753 (submitted 19 Jan 2026). For prime ideals of number fields with alpha in the ring of integers, obtains a higher alpha-Wieferich property implying a nonexistence theorem for higher Wieferich unramified prime ideals, and an equidistribution result for beta-adic digits of alpha^n.
events.revisions: Submitted 19 Jan 2026; further versions not checked.
events.delivers: Nonexistence for higher Wieferich unramified prime ideals in number fields, per the abstract. That is a different object from integer Wieferich primes in base 47.
events.direction: Nonexistence for a number-field analogue; no bearing on integer base-47 existence.

events.what_happened: L. Jones, 'Wieferich Primes and Monogenic Trinomials', arXiv:2605.13460 (v1 13 May 2026; v2 22 May 2026). Shows that x^(2p)+2x^p+2 is monogenic if and only if p is not a Wieferich prime (base 2).
events.delivers: A criterion in base 2: monogenicity equivalent to the non-Wieferich condition for each prime p. States no existence claim.

events.what_happened: G. A. Guedes and R. Nunes Machado Junior, 'Structured Solutions of Prime-Base Binomial Congruences', arXiv:2606.30232 (v1 29 Jun 2026). Studies C(qn, n) ≡ q^n (mod n) for prime base q, and proves that square solutions n = p^2 are exactly governed by Wieferich primes in base q. They report new solutions for q in {2, 3, 5, 7, 11}.
events.delivers: An equivalence for square solutions n = p^2 to the binomial congruence: solution iff p is a base-q Wieferich prime (per abstract). It does not say whether base-q Wieferich primes exist. 47 is prime and would fall under the equivalence, but the abstract computes no base-47 case.
events.remains: Existence of base-47 Wieferich primes, and hence whether base-47 square solutions exist.
events.doubts: Only the abstract page was read. The full text and whether base 47 is treated were not checked.
events.direction: Reformulation: solutions of a congruence correspond to base-q Wieferich primes. No object.

events.what_happened: A. Falk, J. Harrington and L. Jones, 'Generalized Wieferich primes and monogenic trinomials', arXiv:2607.29329 (v1 31 Jul 2026; one version). Defines a generalized Wieferich prime base b as a prime p ≥ 3 with b^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p^2), and generalizes the monogenicity criterion for x^(2n)+bx^n+b to restricted b ≥ 2 and n ≥ 3.
events.delivers: Monogenicity criteria phrased in terms of base-b Wieferich primes, for restricted b and n. No statement on whether base-b Wieferich primes exist for any b. Does not mention base 47.
events.direction: Criteria conditional on the base-b Wieferich condition; no object.

events.what_happened: R. Laniewski, 'Radical defects, Wieferich primes, and the abc conjecture', arXiv:2609.00039 (v1 29 Aug 2026; math.GM). Works mainly in base 2 on the Mersenne line (1, 2^m-1, 2^m). States that an abc counterexample family along that line would require infinitely many Wieferich primes with exponential-order defect growth, and in the introduction extends the identity to every fixed even base g.
events.delivers: A defect identity on a family of triples in base 2 and even bases; it treats infinitude of Wieferich primes as necessary for an abc counterexample family, a conditional-type link, not an existence statement. Base 47 is odd, so the even-base extension as read does not reach it.
events.doubts: A search snippet said the paper extends to rational bases a/b. The HTML version I read (the first 100k of about 179k characters) did not show this, so that claim is unverified. The PDF was unreadable, and the acknowledgments were not visible in the part read.
events.direction: No object; conditional-type link for base-2 triples.

events.what_happened: G. Guedes and R. Machado, 'Perfect numbers, Wieferich primes and the solutions of C(2n,n) ≡ 2^n mod n', arXiv:2609.03091 (v1 2 Sep 2026). Uses SageMath to improve the count of known solutions of the congruence, and states that even perfect numbers and Wieferich primes (base 2) are connected to its solutions. The arXiv page lists a journal reference, Notes on Number Theory and Discrete Mathematics 29 (2023), that predates the posting.
events.revisions: v1 2 Sep 2026 only; the journal reference is dated 2023.
events.delivers: A base-2 link between solutions of a binomial congruence and Wieferich primes. No base-47 content and no existence claim.
events.doubts: The arXiv posting date (2026) and the journal reference (2023) do not agree. Only the abstract page was read, so this was not resolved.

events.what_happened: L. Jones, 'Generalized Wieferich primes and monogenic polynomials', arXiv:2609.13904 (v1 12 Sep 2026). Defines generalized Wieferich primes base b, and proves a monogenicity criterion for another class of trinomials that does not use a Lucas-sequence congruence, extended to N-nomials for N ≥ 4.
events.delivers: A monogenicity criterion stated with base-b Wieferich primes. No existence claim, and base 47 is not mentioned in the abstract.
events.direction: Criterion phrased with the base-b Wieferich condition; no object.

events.what_happened: D. N. Giraudin, 'A counterexample to a conjecture of Thakur on Carlitz-Wieferich primes', arXiv:2607.15305 (v1 14 Jul 2026; v2 22 Jul 2026). Works over F_q[T] with the Carlitz module. The abstract exhibits 'an explicit irreducible c-Wieferich prime of degree 5 over F_{19^3}', refuting a conjecture of Thakur as stated, and says degree 5 is the least possible degree of such a counterexample. Section 6 states that the work was done in collaboration with an AI assistant. This is a function-field analogue, not an integer base.
events.revisions: v1 14 Jul 2026; v2 22 Jul 2026, in which the former exactness statement (Theorem 4.2) was corrected to a conjecture, per an arXiv comment.
events.delivers: A counterexample to a Thakur conjecture on function-field Carlitz-Wieferich primes (c-Wieferich to base 1 in F_q[T]). Restricted to the function-field setting. The v2 change downgrades one claimed exactness theorem to a conjecture.
events.remains: Integer Wieferich primes in any base, including base 47: not touched.

checked_by.who: D. Thakur (named in an arXiv comment)
checked_by.qualification: the arXiv comment does not give the person's role in the field
checked_by.what_they_did: verified the counterexample independently in Magma (per the arXiv comment)

events.directly_checkable: The paper gives an explicit degree-5 prime over F_{19^3}. The PDF was unreadable, so the explicit polynomial was not checked by me.
events.doubts: v2 downgraded a former exactness theorem to a conjecture. The conjectured closed form and the exhaustive-search claim are not proven. The AI-involvement quote comes from a WebFetch summary of the HTML page and was not checked against the paper's own text, because the PDF was unreadable.
events.direction: Cuts against Thakur's conjecture as stated, in the function-field setting. No bearing on integer base 47.
events.object: An explicit irreducible c-Wieferich prime P of degree 5 over F_{19^3} (c-Wieferich to base 1: rho_P(1) ≡ 1 mod P^2), per the abstract. It is a function-field object, not an integer prime p with 47^(p-1) ≡ 1 mod p^2. It is explicit, not a non-constructive existence proof.

events.what_happened: On the erdosproblems.com forum thread for Erdos Problem 11 (is every large odd integer the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2?), a poster with the handle soumya1729 wrote on 24 Jan 2026 that 'I + ChatGPT + Aristotle recently worked through this problem independently', and proposed a conditional implication that would hold if the sum over primes p of 1/ord_{p^2}(2) is finite. Thomas Bloom replied on 25 Jan 2026 that the implication is not in Granville and Soundararajan and is unproven, advised against an arXiv write-up, and said LLM output that looks erroneous will not be shown. Nat Sothanaphan agreed that links to Granville-Soundararajan exist, and said the conditional result seems unlikely to be easy. The thread links the problem to Wieferich primes through Granville-Soundararajan, but concerns base 2 and an additive question, not base 47.
events.revisions: Forum thread with dated posts; no later change to these posts was seen.
events.delivers: Nothing established. A conditional implication, disputed by the forum curator as unproven. It concerns Erdos Problem 11, not the base-47 Wieferich question.
events.remains: Erdos Problem 11 itself is still open according to the thread; base-47 existence is untouched.

disputes.summary: Base-47 search bound. 1.07 x 10^14 (OEIS A278611, 23 Nov 2016) was later given as 2 x 10^14 (Fischer FermQ_Sort.txt, updated 01.09.2025, and an unsigned OEIS A039951 comment). Fischer FermQ_Sorg.txt (updated 30.09.2026) states 'currently searched to 4.75E+12'. A search snippet gave 1.4 x 10^14, which I did not find on any page I opened. Not resolved.

A search snippet attributed to arXiv 2101.08038 (Burrin and Issac, 2021) the remark that base 47 has no known Wieferich prime. The fetched abstract does not mention base 47, and the PDF text was unreadable. Unverified.

summary: The bullet is 'Are there any Wieferich primes in base 47?', a bare existence question. No source I opened reports a prime p with 47^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p^2), and none of the 2026 work on generalized Wieferich primes (Jones, May and September 2026; Falk, Harrington and Jones, July 2026; Guedes and Machado, June and September 2026; Laniewski, August 2026) mentions base 47 or addresses its existence. The only base-47-specific movement is a search bound. OEIS A278611 (23 Nov 2016) gives 1.07 x 10^14, citing Fischer. Fischer's FermQ_Sort.txt (last updated 1 Sep 2025) gives base 47 as 'keine gefunden' (none found) and states that bases with largest prime factor at most 149 are searched to 2.00 x 10^14, which I apply to base 47 by inference. An unsigned OEIS A039951 comment gives the same 2 x 10^14. I could not date when 2 x 10^14 first appeared, so I cannot say whether that step falls inside the window. Fischer's FermQ_Sorg.txt, updated 30 Sep 2026, says bases are 'currently searched to 4.75E+12', which conflicts with 2 x 10^14 and I could not reconcile it. The other number-theory results I found on non-Wieferich primes are conditional on abc or on finiteness assumptions (Fellini and Murty, Aug 2025 to Feb 2026; Graves and Weiss, Mar 2025), or concern prime ideals in number fields (Li and Zhao, Jan 2026), and none asserts a base-47 Wieferich prime. The published base-2 searches (Dorais and Klyve 2011, to 6.7 x 10^15; Carella 2017, to 10^15) are base 2 only. On AI: no source I opened connects an AI system to base 47 or to integer-base Wieferich existence. Two neighbouring events do involve AI. Giraudin's function-field counterexample (arXiv 2607.15305, 14 Jul 2026) credits 'Claude Opus 4.8, Anthropic' as a collaborator in its Section 6; that is a different problem, and the quote comes from a summary of the HTML page. An Erdos Problem 11 forum post (24 Jan 2026) credits ChatGPT and Aristotle with a conditional implication that the forum curator calls unproven. Neither bears on the base-47 bullet. The OpenAI openai/math release (6 Oct 2026) contains no Wieferich manuscript on my reading of its CONTENTS.md: I read it in seven WebFetch chunks, which is a model summary and not a grep. The README summary I read says 719 manuscripts, while secondary coverage says 722; I did not resolve this, and it does not affect the Wieferich check. Several AI-results trackers (Vibe Mathed, Epoch's FrontierMath Erdos benchmark) were searched or partly read and showed no Wieferich entry; Vibe Mathed's page was truncated, so that check is partial. Close call: whether a search bound moved is a judgment about whether the problem's own quantity is the least base-47 Wieferich prime or whether the question is only existence. I recorded the bounds as events, scoped out, so the later pass can make that call.
competing_reading: Read the 2 x 10^14 search as a move in the bound on the least base-47 Wieferich prime, i.e. a quantity the problem's solution would have to lie beyond, and therefore as an event that moved the problem. On the other side: the bullet asks only whether one exists, a finite search with no hit leaves that open, and the 2 x 10^14 figure is itself in doubt, since the same site states 4.75 x 10^12 for its current search and the 2 x 10^14 line has no date. A reader could also take the 2025 and 2026 number-theory papers as moving the problem, but they concern base 2, number fields, or monogenicity criteria, and none claims a base-47 existence result.
what_would_settle_it: An explicit prime p ≠ 47 with 47^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p^2) would settle existence affirmatively, and anyone could check a candidate in seconds with modular exponentiation. A negative answer needs a theorem, not a search, and no method for that appears in any source I read. To pin down the bound: Fischer's search program or a dated statement of which bases were searched to 2 x 10^14, and reconciliation with the 4.75 x 10^12 statement on the 30 Sep 2026 table.
